# Fresh Tomato Salsa and Cooked Sauces

## Raw Pico de Gallo

Pico de gallo is an uncooked tomato sauce made with diced fresh tomatoes, white onion, cilantro,
jalapeno, lime juice, and salt. The ingredients are combined raw to preserve the bright, fresh
flavor of ripe summer tomatoes. Allow the mixture to rest for 15 minutes before serving so the
salt draws out moisture and the flavors meld.

## Cooked Tomato Salsa Roja

For a deeper roasted flavor, char the tomatoes, onion, and dried chiles directly over an open flame
or under the broiler until blistered and softened. Blend the charred vegetables with garlic and
cumin. Simmer the puree in a dry cast iron pan to concentrate and caramelize the flavors.
Season with salt and a small amount of apple cider vinegar to balance acidity.

## Salsa Verde

Green tomatillo-based salsa uses tomatillos, serranos or poblanos, onion, garlic, and cilantro.
Roast or broil the tomatillos until lightly charred. Blend and simmer until the sauce thickens
and turns from bright green to an olive hue, which indicates the raw flavors have cooked off.

## Fermented Hot Sauce

For a complex, tangy hot sauce, ferment whole chiles with salt brine for one to two weeks at room
temperature. The lactobacillus bacteria consume the natural sugars in the chiles, producing lactic
acid that preserves the sauce and adds depth. Blend the fermented chiles with the brine and strain
for a smooth sauce.
